CORRECTION: An earlier version of this receipt (and a message to lead) claimed three environments gave three DIFFERENT King OOFs. That was wrong. It compared the .npz FILE sha256, which is not a content identity: the archive also stores a per-anchor model_sha256 array, and those strings differ between runs while the predictions do not. Comparing the arrays shows P is BITWISE IDENTICAL across all three. What caught it: the rerun legs.npz came out bitwise identical to the first pass, and legs derives KZ from K["P"] values (nc_legs.py L64/L71), so identical legs could only mean identical predictions.
question: does the training environment change the King predictions?
answer: No, not for this step. P: 8,566,057 cells, 0 different, across all three environments.

scheme_source.says: exports NPY_DISABLE_CPU_FEATURES; King uses PV (AMENDMENT 2 moved it from P314); legs uses P314 with OMP=OPENBLAS=1; F10 uses PV with the variable UNSET and OMP=OPENBLAS=2

what_differs: only model_sha256 (the per-anchor LightGBM model file hash): 8143/10333 entries between run1 and run4, 5953/10333 between run3 and run4. The saved model FILES differ while being functionally identical on this data; P is unchanged.
adopted: run4 = PV + NPY_DISABLE_CPU_FEATURES set, because that is what news_chain_resume.sh runs. Aligning with the scheme is still right, but this receipt does NOT claim the first pass produced different predictions -- it did not.
cost_of_my_error: I discarded an F10 pair that had reached 16/23 folds. It was training on the same predictions, so that work was thrown away for nothing. The rerun is still the correct environment, so nothing downstream is wrong; only time was lost.
lesson: a compressed-archive file sha answers "are these files identical", never "did the numbers change". Ask the second question of the arrays, and only of the array you mean.
